notes: Summary: Nebula builds a low-latency, proactive chat product for enterprise customer support. Primary ask: streaming responses with p95 < 120ms for 256-token windows, predictable tail latency at scale (5k concurrent sessions).

Pilot: 6-week POC on Dedicated + Hosted fallback. Ran small pilot with 10k monthly active users simulated traffic. Observed repeated p95 spikes during peak bursts (300-550ms) — streaming glue/jitter and buffer compaction identified.
Quote from CTO: 'We can't risk seeing chat replies lag by half a second during peak support hours.'

Security: Needed SSO/SAML, KMS integration, full audit logs, and EU data residency for part of customer base. Security team put Redwood on hold after audit due to lack of definitive HSM integration timeline.

Decision: Procurement paused by finance (internal budget freeze). Meanwhile Nebula asked about an on-prem alternative; engaged competitor OnPremia who offered an appliance + lower-latency local inference claim.
AE notes: multiple follow-ups (calls + emails) in Oct/Nov; contact became unresponsive after security ticket escalated. Team internally labelled as Closed-Lost (lost to OnPremia) on 2024-11-12.

Technical details gathered: p95 spikes correlated with batching/GC on Dedicated instance type g5-like; streaming path experienced inconsistent chunk boundaries causing client-side reassembly delays. SE proposed kernel tuning and cache warmup; engineering backlog pushed timeline.
One-off asks: deterministic token-level timing traces (we provided), end-to-end trace with their client stub (they could reproduce on competitor).
Notes about champion: initial champion (VP Product) moved to a new role; replacement never fully aligned with business case — contributed to stall.

Suggested next steps if re-engage: offer 8-week targeted perf remediation trial (observability + runtime tuning) with SLA credit and joint perf test plan; escalate HSM/KMS roadmap and provide a signed timeline for on-prem package availability.
